title: Host agent interface
description: What a host's agent definition format actually offers, described independently of this plugin's use of it. This file answers 'what can the host express?'; hosts/<host>.json answers 'how does our role vocabulary map onto it?'. Keeping them apart is the point: the previous conflation is why interface questions were settled by argument instead of by reading. Every claim carries its own provenance, and a claim whose provenance is 'unsourced' may not be depended upon by any role.

retrieved.description: When this interface was last read from its sources. Per-claim provenance carries its own date; this is the date of the whole sweep.

definition.description: How an agent is defined on this host, and where the host looks for it.

format.description: 'none' means the host has no agent definition format that this project could find. It is not a synonym for 'we did not look' - that is what an unsourced provenance says.

locations.description: Paths the host scans, in the host's own convention. Empty where format is 'none'.

fields.description: Every frontmatter or config key the host's agent definition accepts, keyed by the host's own spelling. A key absent from this object is not a key the host lacks - it is a key nobody has sourced. Declare it with supported:false and an unsourced provenance rather than leaving it out, whenever its absence would otherwise be read as evidence.

delegation.description: Whether an agent on this host can dispatch another agent, and whether an agent so dispatched can dispatch in turn. Nested delegation is the capability the orchestrated-worker topology rests on, so it is declared separately from the tool that performs it.

mechanism.description: How delegation is granted or withheld, in the host's own terms. Required when supported is true.

nested.description: Can a dispatched agent dispatch further? 'supported: false' must mean the host documents or demonstrates that it cannot, never that no source was found - use an unsourced provenance for that.

gate.description: What decides whether a given agent may nest.

max_depth.description: A documented hard cap, if the host states one. Null where no cap was sourced. A number repeated by search engines but absent from the host's own material is not a source.

mailbox.description: Whether the host natively carries messages between running agents. Where false, a portable envelope must supply it; where true, reimplementing one duplicates something the host already does better.

notes.description: Free prose that does not fit a field: version skew, migrations, traps. Never load-bearing - nothing reads these.

values.description: The accepted values, where the host documents a closed set. Null where free-form or unsourced. A value observed in somebody's repository is not a documented value; put those in notes.

default.description: What the host does when the key is omitted, stated as behaviour rather than as a literal where the two differ. 'Inherits every tool available to subagents' is the useful form; 'null' is not.

semantics.description: What the key does, in the host's terms. Precedence and interaction with other keys belong here - they are exactly what gets argued about when undeclared.

provenance.description: Where a claim came from and how much weight it bears. The enum is ordered by strength, and the ordering is the point: a claim may only be relied upon at the strength of its weakest supporting source.

level.description: first-party-doc: the vendor's own documentation. first-party-source: the vendor's own code, changelog or schema. empirically-verified: observed directly on the host by this project. corpus-derived: inferred from a sample of real definition files - evidence of what is USED, never of what is SUPPORTED. unsourced: nothing was found; no role may depend on this.

source.description: URL, repository path, or the command whose output was read. Required unless level is unsourced.

quote.description: The source's own words, verbatim. Required for first-party-doc and first-party-source: a paraphrase is where inference re-enters, and re-entering is what this whole file exists to prevent.

sample_size.description: How many real files the inference rests on. Required for corpus-derived.

caveat.description: What would make this claim wrong, or what could not be checked. Recording a known weakness here is always better than omitting the claim.
